title: The Gilded Hollow
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse and the stars vanish in the same night, mercenary Jude Dravenmoor discovers his silent god, Hollow, has been devoured by a rival power that erases memory itself. Trapped inside a country that is being unmade—its roads, records, and recollections dissolving into the Gilded Hollow—Jude must lead a ragged band of survivors along smuggler's roads that exist only because he remembers them. His loyalty to his dead god's last command collides with the truth that Hollow engineered its own death to trap the devourer. In the end, Jude chooses truth over faith: he speaks Hollow's true name aloud, unmaking both gods, and walks out of Thornfell carrying nothing but the memories he refuses to surrender.
about_author: Wendell Whitlock is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about borders, oaths, and the people who live in the gaps between them.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Jude Dravenmoor's POV. Guiding a smuggler's caravan through the Thornfell passes, Jude feels his god Hollow go silent just as every star above the mountains vanishes at once. The border wards shatter like glass behind him. The beat is dread: the world he trusted has stopped existing, and he felt it happen.

chapters.title: A Country With No Edges
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Descending into the valley town of Bellharrow, he finds maps blank, boundary stones smooth, and townsfolk unable to say what nation they live in. A ward-scribe named Sera Vey recruits him: something is eating Thornfell's definition. The beat is disorientation sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Catechism
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with flashback. Jude recalls how Hollow first spoke to him through an oath sworn over stolen goods, and realizes the old smuggler's prayers were memory-rituals keeping the passes real. He tests one on a fading road—and it holds. The beat is fragile hope built on profane foundations.

chapters.title: What Sera Buried
chapters.summary: Sera Vey's POV. Sera confesses she helped build the wards and hid a flaw in them years ago to spite her superiors; the devourer entered through her crack. Guilt-ridden, she gives Jude a shard of ward-glass that shows what a place used to be. The beat is guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the mining town of Graysink, survivors worship the silence where Hollow used to be, singing hymns to keep their names from slipping away. Their blind priest recognizes Jude as 'the god-sworn' and begs him to lead them out. The beat is the weight of being mistaken for salvation.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember Me
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Leading the choir north, Jude discovers the smuggler's roads persist only where his memories of them are strong—but each use burns a memory away. He forgets his mother's face to save thirty lives. The beat is sacrifice made literal and arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Gilded Man
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The devourer manifests: a figure of beaten gold wearing Hollow's face, who offers each survivor their happiest memory back in exchange for the rest. Two choir members accept and walk into it smiling. The beat is seduction—the enemy is generous.

chapters.title: Oathbreaker's Bridge
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At a bridge that exists only for those who have never broken an oath, the group fractures; Sera cannot cross, and Jude lies about why he can. Crossing alone, he finds the far side already half-eaten. The beat is isolation—the cost of small dishonesties.

chapters.title: Letters to a Silent God
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, epistolary interlude. Camped in a chapel that no longer believes in itself, Jude writes letters to Hollow demanding answers, burning each one. The last page answers back in his own handwriting. The beat is grief curdling toward suspicion.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera leads them to the Undercroft, a vault where Thornfell stored its official memory: treaties, censuses, executed prisoners' final words. It is intact but guarded by a warden made of redacted text. The beat is awe shadowed by institutional rot.

chapters.title: The Prisoner's Name
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Bargaining with the warden, Jude learns the devourer was once a person—a condemned man whose name the state erased so thoroughly that only hunger remained. Hollow helped write the sentence. The beat is horror at justice's machinery.

chapters.title: Winter Falls Early
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. The long winter begins mid-autumn, freezing the fading roads solid; supplies fail and the choir votes to abandon Sera as a curse-bringer. Jude vetoes them with the last of his authority. The beat is leadership fraying under cold and fear.

chapters.title: What I Forgot at Bellharrow
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera deciphers her own hidden flaw and realizes the wards were never meant to keep things out—they were a cage, built by Hollow, holding the devourer inside Thornfell. The country isn't collateral damage; it's the prison wall. The beat is betrayal recontextualized.

chapters.title: The God Who Lied First
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Confronting the gilded figure directly, Jude learns Hollow's silence wasn't death but strategy: Hollow let itself be swallowed to poison the devourer from within, dooming Thornfell as acceptable loss. Every prayer Jude ever made was a brick in the cage. The beat is faith breaking against truth.

chapters.title: Deserter's Road
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Half the choir deserts toward a rumored southern gate that Jude knows is already eaten. He lets them go, keeping only those willing to hear the truth. The beat is release—loyalty freely chosen rather than commanded.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera finds it: the Undercroft's founding charter contains a door written into existence before Thornfell had borders—an exit predating the cage. But opening it requires a name the state erased, spoken by someone who remembers it. The beat is a plan with an impossible price.

chapters.title: Remembering the Unremembered
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In Hollow's abandoned shrine, Jude performs the smuggler's rites backward, feeding his own memories into the void until fragments surface: the condemned man's trial, his face, his name—Merrick Vale. Jude loses his childhood to hold onto it. The beat is terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Long Dark March
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The remnant crosses the frozen heart of Thornfell toward the Undercroft while the Gilded Hollow closes around them like a fist, offering each traveler their dearest lie. They walk holding hands and speaking each other's names aloud. The beat is solidarity against oblivion.

chapters.title: Two Gods, One Grave
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the Undercroft's threshold, the gilded figure offers Jude everything back—Hollow restored, the stars relit—if he keeps Merrick Vale's name silent forever. Jude sees the trap: mercy as the final lock. The beat is temptation at its most sincere.

chapters.title: The True Name Spoken
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax. Before the assembled survivors, Jude speaks 'Merrick Vale' aloud and then Hollow's true name beside it, unbinding god and devourer together. Thornfell's remaining edges dissolve; the door opens onto ordinary starlight. The beat is catharsis—truth as the only clean weapon.

chapters.title: Exiles From a Map
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The survivors step through into neighboring lands that have never heard of Thornfell, stateless and unrecorded. Sera begins writing its history from the shard of ward-glass, naming streets and dead aloud. The beat is mourning transformed into authorship.

chapters.title: The Roads I Kept
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, resolution. Years later, Jude guides caravans through foreign mountains, teaching young smugglers the old rites—not to any god, but so the roads stay remembered. He has forgotten Hollow entirely, and sleeps well. The beat is peace earned by letting go.
